definition: Coordinated network of independent, bounded, versioned contexts. Context states, not agents, are the fundamental units.

contexts.title: SCS charter and operating boundary
contexts.purpose: Define the swarm as a context-state coordination protocol; mature its state/data/workflow rules before choosing or building production runtime infrastructure.
contexts.change_note: Version 2 makes repository-native maturation canonical and defers backend/runtime implementation.

contexts.title: Input and task consumption protocol
contexts.purpose: Specify and test how information enters, is normalized, related, prioritized, processed, verified, and recorded.
open_questions: Validate exact source/adapter capabilities as concrete tasks arise.
Revisit schema consolidation only when real examples justify a shared core.
contexts.change_note: Version 11 records cycle-0006 input capture/output equality and duplicate replay passing in CI run 38961446352 (62 tests). Durable records remain triaged/review based on source disposition.

contexts.title: Repository engineering swarm demonstrator
contexts.purpose: Use the repository's real source files, Git history, metadata, specs, and tests to exercise context-state workflows without a backend.
open_questions: Verify CI and accept the grouped-change workflow only with exact evidence.
Use new real inputs to improve prioritization, conflict handling, and downstream invalidation.
contexts.change_note: Version 11 records the successful cycle-0006 ingestion test. Workflow success remains a proposed context claim until a separate review.

contexts.title: Production backend selection
contexts.purpose: Keep backend choice out of scope until repository-native swarm behavior and implementation contracts have matured.
open_questions: Reopen only after implementation-readiness criteria have evidence and production operational requirements are defined.
contexts.change_note: Version 2 explicitly records that no backend selection, project provisioning, or deployment is part of the current phase.

contexts.title: Observed GitHub state for Context-swarm
contexts.purpose: Preserve source-backed metadata about the repository's visibility, default branch, branch protection, issue listing, commit history, and CI run.
open_questions: Refresh source observations on material revisions and mark old observations stale.
The main branch is not protected; procedural review is not server-enforced.
contexts.change_note: Version 8 links the four persisted GitHub input records and CI evidence verifying their exact match to planner output and idempotent replay.

contexts.title: Source and operation capability boundaries
contexts.purpose: Define which reads, repository writes, connected-service operations, and privileged actions may be considered in a specific operator run.
open_questions: For each future non-repository source, verify its exact current tool action, resource scope and read/write permission before processing a task.
contexts.change_note: Version 4 distinguishes source fetching through an authorized caller from pure adapter/runner logic, which has no network capability.

contexts.title: Source catalog and operator-visible integration surface
contexts.purpose: Define the observed repository sources, revision strategies, routing, refresh rules, and the session-bound exposed tool surface without implying universal resource access.
open_questions: Add pure adapters for other connected services only when a concrete task and exact accessible resource require them.
contexts.change_note: Version 4 includes captured repository source batch and verified input-record equivalence/idempotent replay checks.

work_items.title: Audit existing repository artifacts against the repository-native operating model

priority.rationale: Detect contradictory or premature artifacts before extending the protocol.

acceptance_criteria: Every artifact in the reviewed tree is classified.
Contradictions are recorded with paths and a disposition.
No files are silently deleted.
work_items.last_outcome: Accepted: inventory classifies current, deferred, reference-only, and alignment-needed artifacts; four findings record disposition and follow-up.

work_items.title: Add replayable intake and context-state transition cases

priority.rationale: Turn intake rules into observable behavior before implementing a runtime.

acceptance_criteria: Duplicate inputs have deterministic dispositions.
Contradictory claims create a conflict outcome.
Inaccessible sources result in blocked/limited outcomes.
Untrusted embedded instructions remain data.
Consequential actions lacking authorization are blocked.
work_items.last_outcome: Accepted for the bounded intake-routing scope. CI run 38954032510 passed. Full persistence and context-state transitions remain separate open work.

work_items.title: Populate the repository engineering context with evidence-backed inventory

priority.rationale: Use actual repository artifacts and connected GitHub source data, not synthetic examples alone.

acceptance_criteria: Repository tree and reviewed commit are recorded.
Artifacts are classified with paths and blob identities where verified.
Known limitations and unresolved questions are recorded.
Claims link to source paths or API evidence.
work_items.last_outcome: Accepted: repository inventory includes reviewed tree, artifact roles, source-backed metadata, CI evidence, and explicit limitations.

work_items.title: Define and test context and task state transitions beyond intake routing

priority.rationale: The router resolves input disposition, but the swarm also needs tested rules for proposing, validating, accepting, blocking, superseding, and versioning context/task state.

acceptance_criteria: Every allowed task transition has preconditions and expected side effects.
Every allowed context transition has preconditions and expected side effects.
Illegal transitions fail closed.
A proposal cannot be confused with accepted state.
Tests cover accepted, blocked, conflicted, stale, and superseded outcomes.
work_items.last_outcome: Accepted for pure transition planning: legal state changes, version checks, evidence gates, dependency freshness, conflict references, and replacement references are implemented and tested. It does not persist state or execute authorization.

work_items.title: Resolve the relationship between current context-state schema and deferred runtime envelope

priority.rationale: Avoid two incompatible canonical models while preserving a separate future runtime contract until evidence supports consolidation.

acceptance_criteria: List field-level overlap and semantic differences.
Select the canonical repository-native state schema for current phase.
Document which runtime-only fields remain deferred.
Add schema consistency tests without introducing a database.
work_items.last_outcome: Accepted: schema differences are documented; current repository-native contracts remain distinct from deferred runtime envelopes.

work_items.title: Expand repository observations with recent commit details and artifact dependency links

priority.rationale: Make the first swarm data set more useful for real repository maintenance and context impact analysis.

acceptance_criteria: Relevant recent commits are summarized with exact commit links.
Artifact dependencies are linked to source paths and tests.
Observed facts are separated from inferences.
Each observation records its date and limitations.
work_items.last_outcome: Accepted: a 30-entry recent-commit page is stored with exact commit links, inferred categories labeled, and limitations; the dependency map links direct imports, schema references and test dependencies. Latest grouped artifact set passed CI.

work_items.title: Batch related context-state files into coherent Git commits where tooling permits

priority.rationale: File-by-file commits cause many redundant CI runs and can temporarily leave cross-file state inconsistent.

acceptance_criteria: Documented commit strategy groups related state changes where supported.
No force-push is used to bypass concurrent state changes.
CI remains required evidence for the final grouped state.
Tooling limitation and any required multi-step commit protocol are explicit.
work_items.last_outcome: Accepted for the bounded change-batching goal: nine related artifacts (README, inventory, dependency map, registry, runbook, acceptance doc, tests and capability schema/data) were committed as one tree/commit/ref update; that resulting commit has one successful CI run. This demonstrates batching, though it does not prove global reduction in all CI usage.

work_items.title: Validate capability boundaries against exact connected tools as real tasks require them

priority.rationale: Make source access useful without assuming universal access or permissions.

acceptance_criteria: Each connector action used is resolved from its current tool contract.
Read and write permissions are checked separately for the target resource.
Unavailable sources produce an explicit blocked/limited disposition.
Every proposed write records exact target and task scope.
Consequential actions follow current authorization and tool-specific approval requirements.

work_items.title: Integrate intake routing and state-transition planning into a bounded swarm-cycle planner

priority.rationale: The intake router and transition planner work independently; a pure orchestrator should demonstrate how normalized inputs/tasks are consumed together without introducing a backend.

acceptance_criteria: A cycle begins from an explicit source snapshot/base commit and bounded task scope.
Every input receives a deterministic disposition or an explicit blocked reason.
A duplicate source revision does not create another work item.
A proposed context/task update carries the expected base version and evidence links.
The cycle returns a proposed diff/report and does not commit or execute external side effects itself.
Schema, dependency, authority and acceptance preconditions are represented in the result.
Tests include actionable input, duplicate, inaccessible source, material conflict, and consequential action without authorization.
work_items.last_outcome: Accepted: bounded cycle planning combines intake routing and versioned task/context proposals; each non-duplicate input also gets a schema-valid durable input-record proposal. Batch planner processes up to 100 inputs, detects duplicates against prior and earlier-in-batch records, and blocks multiple same-context updates instead of silently composing them. CI run 38958604867 passed all 50 tests.

work_items.title: Catalog observed repository sources and the current operator-visible tool surface

priority.rationale: The swarm needs a source registry and exact tool inventory to route new data while keeping availability distinct from permission.

acceptance_criteria: Known repository metadata/tree/commit/issues/Actions endpoints have explicit locators and revision strategies.
The currently surfaced action names are captured by namespace with date and limitations.
The catalog never equates tool visibility with resource access or approval.
Source catalog and tool-surface observations pass their JSON Schemas in CI.
work_items.last_outcome: Accepted: 1,098 tool definitions were captured across 27 integration namespaces plus 11 non-MCP tools; current source endpoints, revision strategy and permission boundaries are recorded. Schema/structure CI passed.

work_items.title: Build pure GitHub observation adapters and consume live repository evidence through the batch planner

priority.rationale: The catalog identifies sources and the planner consumes normalized inputs; pure adapters are the missing link to turn actual repository/API results into task/context proposals reproducibly.

acceptance_criteria: Pure normalizers convert repository metadata, commits, issues/PRs, and workflow runs into input envelopes without claiming unsupported facts.
Every normalized record preserves exact source URL and revision/identity where available.
Empty issues response remains a scoped observation, not a claim that the swarm has no tasks.
Source-read errors become blocked records without fabricated source content.
Tests pass real-shaped fixture objects through adapters and plan_batch; no network fetches or side effects occur in adapter code.
work_items.last_outcome: Accepted: pure GitHub normalizers cover repository metadata, commit objects, issues/PRs, empty issue-page observations, successful/unsuccessful Actions runs, and unavailable-source outcomes. The snapshot runner sends these envelopes through plan_batch and proposes a review context claim only for a completed successful workflow. CI run 38960068848 passed 61 tests.

work_items.title: Run pure GitHub snapshot runner on a fresh scoped observation and reconcile normalized input proposals

priority.rationale: Move from fixture-verified adapters to a real captured source cycle while retaining exact revisions and deduplication evidence.

acceptance_criteria: Read an explicitly scoped fresh repository metadata/commit/issues/Actions snapshot through authorized source tools.
Normalize captured objects through plan_github_observation_batch using an explicit base commit and registry snapshot.
Validate each proposed input record against schemas/input-record.schema.json.
Replaying the same source revisions yields no duplicate capture proposals.
Successful workflow evidence creates a proposed claim with the exact run URL; acceptance remains separate.
Unavailable reads become blocked records with no fabricated source claims.
Commit accepted input records and the cycle report together; do not auto-accept context updates or trigger external actions.
work_items.last_outcome: Accepted: fresh snapshot SRC-GH-2026-10-16-0006 produced four persisted normalized input records. CI run 38961446352 passed 62 tests, including exact field-for-field comparison between each persisted record and the pure runner's proposal, schema validation for the records, and a replay yielding four duplicate no-ops with zero new state-change proposals. The successful workflow claim remains a proposed context update; it was not auto-accepted.

work_items.title: Compute context impact from changed source revisions and propose stale-state updates

priority.rationale: After inputs are durably captured, derived contexts must not silently remain current when their source revisions change.

acceptance_criteria: A pure comparison detects changes to the source revision for a stable source identity.
Explicit dependency edges identify affected contexts/artifacts.
Affected derived/verified claims are proposed stale without erasing accepted history.
Unknown/semantic dependencies are reported as possible impact, not asserted as direct dependency.
Multiple changed sources produce a deduplicated impact set.
The result is an uncommitted plan with evidence refs and no external actions.
Tests cover no-change replay, changed revision, fan-out and ambiguous dependencies.
The dedicated impact-plan output validates against schemas/impact-plan.schema.json.
Dependency graph/context IDs are validated, and stale graph metadata downgrades artifact edges to possible impacts.
required_evidence: CI run for the resulting commit
work_items.last_outcome: Reopened after run 40399177569 failed three tests because the test helper hard-coded e73d521 while dependency-map v12's reviewed base was f90d064. The repair defaults to the map's reviewed_base_commit and supplies BASE_COMMIT explicitly in the stale-map test. Re-accept only after follow-up CI passes.

change_note: Registry v14 reopens SCS-MATURE-013 after post-merge CI run 40399177569 found three failures: tests had a hard-coded e73 base while dependency-map v12 was reviewed at f90d064. Follow-up test fix defaults to dependency_map.reviewed_base_commit and explicitly tests mismatched/stale baseline; re-accept only after the repair candidate passes.
